computed_prediction_at_realized_mean.claim: 7.5x concurrent-sequence capacity at fixed VRAM for sequences of 258 tokens (4,300 paged vs 571 contiguous), against a baseline that reserves max_seq=2048 tokens per request. The ratio is a function of sequence length and falls to ~1x as lengths approach 2048.

derivation: baseline              B3 — contiguous KVCacheGPU(max_seq=2048) per request (engine/scheduler.py:16,26-27)
bytes per sequence    2048 tokens x 32,768 B = 67,108,864 B (64 MiB) — reserved in full at admission, regardless of tokens actually used
caveat                the engine is single-request today; this is what its ALLOCATION STRATEGY supports concurrently, which is the S1 comparison
model                 16L/8kvh/64d/2B: 16 layers, 8 kv heads, head_dim 64, 2 bytes/element
bytes per token       2 (K,V) x 16 x 8 x 64 x 2 = 32,768 B (32 KiB)
bytes per block       16 tokens x 32,768 B = 524,288 B (512 KiB)
tokens capacity       73,109 blocks x 16 tokens = 1,169,744 tokens
bytes left unused     419,431 B (< one block, by construction)
notes: Sized from the CLI VRAM budget; measured device figures are in `gpu`.

Length-independent by construction.

name: capacity_s1
notes: MEASURED: sequences admitted through BlockAllocator/SequenceBlocks until can_allocate() refused. COMPUTED: the contiguous baseline B3, which cannot be measured because the engine is single-request (engine/scheduler.py, module docstring).

The ratio is a function of sequence length. It is 7.7x at realized mean length 258, and tends to 1x as lengths approach max_seq=2048. Quoting it without this distribution attached is not a defensible claim.

Computed prediction at the realized mean (258 tokens): 4,300 paged sequences, ratio 7.5x. Divergence from the measured 4,406 / 7.7x is the effect of length SKEW, which a mean-based calculation cannot capture.
